notes.orderCostDesc: Cards burn about ₹5,800 a month at 40%. A gold pledge at 12% on ₹2.2 lakh burns about ₹2,200. Gold first costs roughly ₹3,600 a month — a defensible price for protecting family gold, as long as it is a choice and not an accident.
notes.orderCallout: Ask first: ₹2.2 lakh borrowed against ₹10 lakh of gold is 22% loan-to-value, where lenders go to 75%. Partial repayment should free far more gold than it costs. If partial release works, you protect the gold and clear the cards, and the trade-off disappears.
notes.cardConvertNote: ₹1,74,671 at ~40% costs ₹69,900 a year. The same balance at 15% on a bank EMI plan costs ₹26,200. Four phone calls, ₹43,700 a year. The highest return per hour anywhere in this file.
notes.goldBufferNote: Releasing ₹70,000 a month as an EMI backstop will get you through a bad month, and it is also how family gold becomes permanently pledged. Set a written cap on total gold pledged at any one time, and attach a repayment date to every draw before you take it. A buffer without an exit date is not a buffer.
